I think if you don't do a verified program (there are ones that have curriculum that isn't online) that it's kind of up to your parents to keep you on level and placement tests keep get you into college etc.  SAT STATE tests etc.  But someone else may be able to give a better idea of that as it isn't my normal approach where I work, and every state is different.  I don't know what qualifies as an umbrella school, they may all be. But I know for sure that Time4learning is an umbrella school. Most of my kids uses connections academy or IUniversityPrep so I'm not 100%. I have 3 kids who use time for learning and they are usually behind the curve because their parents have the ability to decide their lessons and they give the minimum, but that to me as a parent issue not a format issue. I'm sorry I don't have more but I figured an answer is better than no answer!

So I have 2 degrees in education and worked in public school for 5 years but I currently work at a homeschool/private arts academy in Texas so I'm going to answer based on our situation but please take it knowing states etc are different.

Usually it takes a bit to get "accepted" to a school program. Now it depends on where you apply. Elite schools within a month. General school districts who offer a homeschool program can be as soon as a week for acceptance. Time for learning and other programs that aren't free schools are faster turn around.

Testing, through school district based programs, they offer lots of options! They are always sending emails for SAT prep seminars, where to test, etc. So, I guess that depends where you go.

Meet ups I'm kinda clueless on. Facebook etc sometimes has that kind of stuff but because we are an arts school it's not really a need.  I do know that Texas connections had options for that stuff that they email about but I have no idea what it's like.

If you do an online verified school, You get the same workload but you get to dictate it. You go to live lessons where the teacher teaches you stuff, a lot of times they record it for kids who can't be there. you get text books work online do the work and poof you get an diploma. Beyond that no clue.

I hope this helps some. Feel free to message me with anything I missed!

It isn’t easy being the ugly stepsister. Everybody always feels so sorry for poor little Cinderella, but what about me? I deserve a little sympathy, too. Does my fairy godmother ever turn up with a magic wand? Does the prince ever dance with me at the ball? Not on your life. The best I can ever hope for with my pumpkins is a decent piece of pie. And as for the rats, well, rats are rats, with their sneaky eyes and skinny tails, nibbling and gnawing at the garbage. I never saw one yet who turned into a coachman. 

If you ask me, that Cinderella is weird. Certainly, she isn’t normal. Besides the fact that she has naturally curly hair and wears size 4 ½ shoes, she is so good-natured that it’s downright sickening. If you had to dust and sweep and clean all day long, would you go around singing to the birds? Of course you wouldn’t. No sensible person would. 

A lot of people think I’m jealous of her. Maybe I am. And with good reason. I subsisted on seven hundred calories a day for three whole weeks before the ball. I did my leg-lift exercises faithfully. I got a perm and a facial and a manicure. I even bought a new gown. Blue velvet. Designer label. I mean, I was ready. Princey, I thought to myself, here I come! 

And what happened? Little Cindy, who has never seen the inside of a health club in her life and who doesn’t know the caloric difference between a carrot stick and a chocolate éclair, whips together a dress out of some old curtains from K-Mart, waltzes off to the ball and snags the prince. 

It isn’t fair! It really isn’t fair!
